d_class_hs_position: US 3921.19.0000 stable/high; EU 8507.90.31 stable/high; India 3921.19.90 stable/medium. Divergence is explicit and preserved.

aa_classification_candidate.divergence_note: US/India classify as Chapter 39 cellular plastics; EU classifies as Chapter 85 battery separator under a binding carve-out for <40μm films.

open_question_for_d_ruling: Should this separator divergence remain a permanent jurisdiction-specific split, or is there later India-side or international authority strong enough to justify moving India off the current Chapter 39 route or reframing the divergence for downstream legal guidance?
founder_override_note: Founder-approved temporary provenance bridge for missing Indian primary case texts discussing separator treatment. EY and PwC secondary summaries are accepted for the test run only and must be replaced when the underlying India judgments/orders are acquired.

secondary_authority_sources.source: PwC Customs & Trade Newsletter / Case law collation
secondary_authority_sources.citation: Exide Industries Ltd. v. Commissioner of Customs (2007)
secondary_authority_sources.holding_summary: Battery separators in roll form treated as parts of accumulators rather than plastic articles, providing secondary support for a competing Chapter 85 route.

secondary_authority_sources.source: PwC Customs & Trade Newsletter / Case law collation
secondary_authority_sources.citation: HBL Nife Power Systems Ltd. v. Commissioner of Customs (2012)
secondary_authority_sources.holding_summary: Followed Exide and treated battery separators as accumulator parts, reinforcing the existence of a live India-side Chapter 85 counter-signal.

jurisdiction_divergence_detail.ruling_a: CBP HQ 967313; India material-first Chapter 39 route
jurisdiction_divergence_detail.ruling_b: EU Commission Note C/2025/6096 + EU CN Regulation 2025/1926
